test_title: PYST 3: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:

Finger in the pie

options.text: Being involved or interfering in something

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "Being involved or interfering in something". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Finger in the pie"** means being involved in or interfering with something, typically in a way that is considered intrusive or unnecessary. (किसी चीज में शामिल होना या हस्तक्षेप करना) • **Example:** She has her finger in every pie at work, always trying to manage everything herself. • The correct meaning of "Finger in the pie" is being involved or interfering in something. (किसी चीज में हस्तक्षेप करना) • **Example:** He has his finger in the pie of every major project in the company. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "Being involved or interfering in something". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 2:** Trying to cause conflict intentionally (जानबूझकर संघर्ष पैदा करने की कोशिश करना). • **Example:** He was accused of trying to cause conflict intentionally among his colleagues. • **Option 3:** Avoiding responsibility (जिम्मेदारी से बचना). • **Example:** She keeps avoiding responsibility by blaming others for her mistakes. • **Option 4:** Speaking without knowledge (ज्ञान के बिना बोलना). • **Example:** He often speaks without knowledge, which leads to misunderstandings. 4d:T6da, The correct answer is** option 1.**
